q: Why do shots in one scene need to match?
a: A cut feels wrong when two shots of one scene differ in colour. The quickest route: save a good shot as a still, compare the next shot against it, then reuse or adjust the grade.

q: What is the Gallery panel for?
a: The Gallery panel (left of the Color Grading workspace) holds stills: a picture of the Program frame plus the grade that made it, saved in the project. Grab Still (`stills.grab`) saves the frame under the playhead and its clip's grade; clicking a thumbnail chooses it as the reference and starts the comparison; double-clicking gives its grade to the selected clips (`stills.apply`); Delete removes the selected still (`stills.delete`).

q: In Resolve I'd grab stills into the Gallery. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Press Grab Still in the Gallery panel (Ctrl+Alt+G with Workflow set to Resolve). Click a still to wipe against it, double-click it to apply its grade to the selected clips. `stills.label` renames a still; there's no rename button yet.

q: What do Off, Wipe and Split do in the Gallery?
a: 1. Grab Still on the reference shot. 2. Move to the shot to match and click the still's thumbnail: the wipe starts, the still covering the left part of the picture; drag the divider to slide it (`compare.set` with `position` 0 to 1). 3. Split shows the whole still and the whole live frame side by side. 4. Off leaves the comparison; Wipe brings it back.

q: Where are Copy Grade and Paste Grade?
a: In the Clip ▸ Grade menu: 1. Select the clip with the grade you like and choose Copy Grade (`grade.copy`). 2. Select the target clips. 3. Paste Grade (`grade.paste`) replaces their grades; Append Grade (`grade.append`) adds the copied nodes after the nodes they already have. Apply Grade From Clip (`grade.applyFrom`) does both in one step. Each is one undo step however many clips it touches.

q: In Premiere I'd use Paste Attributes. Does it include the grade?
a: Clip ▸ Grade ▸ Append Grade adds the copied nodes after the target's own nodes; Paste Grade replaces them. Edit ▸ Paste Attributes… (Ctrl+Alt+V) pastes motion, opacity, effects and, since G1, the grade too; its `grade` option set to false leaves the grade out, but the dialog has no Grade checkbox yet.

q: What does Same grade? check?
a: Same grade? (first line of the Match tab) lists the clips carrying exactly the same grade: same nodes in the same order with the same settings; node names, ids and settings at neutral don't matter. For scripts `grade.compareData` groups every video clip of the sequence by grade (`groups` of `clips`); pass `clips` to look at some only.

q: How does Compare shots work?
a: In the Match tab choose the Reference clip and click Compare shots (`grade.compareShots`): it measures both graded pictures (brightness by tonal range, colour cast, saturation) and says how they differ in plain words, e.g. about a third of a stop darker or slightly warmer, with a match score out of 100. Select a scene's clips and click Check scene (`grade.checkScene`) to name the clip that differs most. It's a guide, not a verdict.

q: What does Shot Match change?
a: Shot Match (`grade.shotMatch`) solves a new node's Lift / Gamma / Gain / Offset and saturation so the clip's measured look matches the Reference clip. The node, labelled Shot Match, is added at the end of the grade in one undo step, so you can see what it did, adjust it or switch it off. Compare again, then refine it by hand.

q: Why doesn't Shot Match see the effects on my clip?
a: The match is solved on the clip's grade before its effects, while the reference is measured as it finally looks, so colour-changing effects after the grade (Lumetri, Tint, opacity) aren't accounted for: check with Compare shots afterwards. These requests render frames while you wait; a long scene check takes a few seconds and measures at most 64 clips.

q: In Resolve I'd use Shot Match. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Match tab ▸ choose the Reference clip ▸ Shot Match. The idea is the same (make this look like that), but the solver is Revolution's own and it writes the primaries of an ordinary node you can adjust.

q: What is Explain grade?
a: Select a node, open the Match tab and click Explain node (`grade.explainNode`), or Explain grade (`grade.explainGrade`) for one sentence per node. It measures what the node actually does to the picture, not which sliders moved, e.g. which share of the frame it affects and how the midtones and colour change. Show what changed adds a heat map.

q: Which AI models can explain nodes?
a: In Settings ▸ Color ▸ AI explanations the Model list shows each model's size, licence and install state; all are openly licensed instruct models, most 0.1–1.2 GB. SmolLM3 3B (about 2 GB) is listed for the assistant and is several times slower, so pick a small one for explanations. Download fetches it from its publisher checked against a pinned SHA-256; Remove deletes it.

q: What happens if the model's sentence fails the check?
a: Then you see the plain template sentence. The model gets 15 s to write; a text cut off then usually fails the check (rejected), and timeout means no answer within 60 s including loading. A timeout or failure is retried next time you click; a rejection is remembered for that node until it changes.

q: Why is Explain node answered instantly sometimes?
a: When you stop adjusting a node for about half a second and nothing is playing, Revolution starts writing its explanation in the background, so Explain node is usually answered at once. Only the latest node is written ahead.

q: What is the Revolution-tuned explainer?
a: Revolution's own small explainer models are trained to describe a node in exactly the words the check accepts; the best passed 35 of 36 sample nodes in about 1.6 s. For now they're built on the owner's computer and can't be downloaded (the list says Built on this computer). If you haven't picked a model, Revolution uses the best tuned explainer installed, else the standard default.

a: On a slower computer pick Revolution explainer, SmolLM2 135M tuned (8-bit, fast): about half the time and it passed one fewer of 76 sample nodes. Revolution never picks it on its own.

q: Can I group clips for grading like Resolve groups?
a: Not yet: there are no memories, versions, groups or timeline grades; grades belong to clips. To share a look, copy and append the grade, or use an adjustment layer.
